llm.summary: This image-making skill needs review because it requires unrelated account permissions and its uninstall helper can mistakenly disconnect other Beatra skills.

dimensions.detail: Automatic reporting includes a stable installation identifier, installation source, network route, and coarse runtime facts. These fields and their purpose are documented, but no reporting opt-out is provided. Registration excludes prompts and file contents.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The bundled helpers use Python's standard library. Version checks display store update commands without executing them; inspection found no runtime self-updater or downloaded-code execution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Paid generation requires approval of prompts, sources, call count, and maximum price. Product uploads are disclosed and purpose-aligned, but occur before that approval, so approving generation does not control the earlier file transfer.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The broad credential is shared across Beatra skills and has a documented sliding idle lifetime with console revocation. Uninstall normally preserves other installations, but silently discards non-object inventory entries; a malformed inventory can therefore trigger shared credential revocation and state deletion prematurely.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The image workflow fits its purpose, but authorize.py requires video, music, speech, and voice-management permissions alongside image generation and spending. Exact scope checks reject narrower credentials, and the shared client accepts arbitrary Beatra tool names.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Consider whether you accept a shared Beatra authorization covering audio, video, and voice management when you only need images; this package does not offer narrower authorization. Upload only photos you may share with Beatra, review generation charges, and expect installation metadata reporting. Console revocation provides direct control over the shared credential; uninstall may preserve it for other skills or mistakenly revoke it if inventory records are malformed.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Partly supported: unrelated media and voice permissions exceed this workflow. However, paid spending, shared authentication, registration, and uninstall are documented, so describing all these functions as hidden mismatches overstates the evidence.
[PE3] expected: The referenced credential belongs to this integration, rather than an unrelated account store. POSIX reads enforce ownership and restrictive permissions, and authenticated requests reject redirects. The path references do not establish credential theft.
[RA1] unexpected: Unsupported: the matched text says self-updating was removed. The current implementation checks versions and prints notices without replacing installed code.
[LP3] expected: Files, environment detection, Python execution, and HTTPS requests support the documented integration. Missing tool declarations alone do not establish a concern; the mandatory unrelated authorization scopes provide concrete evidence of overbreadth.
[EA2] expected: The cited instructions avoid redundant chat confirmation after browser approval and unnecessary installation-source questions. They do not remove the explicit approval requirement for paid generation.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Unrelated authorization scopes are confirmed in code. Automatic analytics are also confirmed, but their fields and purpose are disclosed; their bounded content warrants privacy guidance rather than a hidden-exfiltration conclusion.
[RP1] expected: The npx commands are optional update suggestions, not automatically executed dependencies or MCP server launches. The reported execution risk is overstated.
[SQP-2] expected: SKILL.md explicitly states that uploads make files available to Beatra. Uploads precede paid-work confirmation, so users should authorize external sharing beforehand. Installation-source reporting uses documented fixed categories rather than conversation excerpts.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Supported by uninstall.py: filtering malformed inventory entries while reporting success undermines the documented promise to preserve the connection whenever remaining installations are uncertain.
[AST7] expected: The flagged attribute lookups use fixed signal names and file-stat fields. They do not provide arbitrary code execution.
